hypothesis: n003 is fit with pointwise BCE, whose gradient is dominated by getting each impression's absolute probability right across the whole corpus, but the metric never compares two users' scores: GAUC integrates within-user pairwise orderings and nDCG@5 only reads the top of each user's list. BPR replaces that global likelihood with an explicit within-user positive-vs-sampled-negative margin, so every gradient step moves exactly the comparison the metric charges for, and with the five official fields held identical (k=16, lr=0.001) the only thing changing is the objective. The screen-tier ablation of n003 already showed loss:pairwise as the single positive component (+0.001734 at capped epochs), and I claim that is budget-suppressed rather than at ceiling because BPR needs more passes to see enough sampled pairs per user; at full tier I predict primary >= 0.6036 (>= +0.002 over 0.6016), with the gain concentrated in activity_q3/q4 (long lists give many informative in-user pairs) and in pop_q1/pop_q2 where n003 is weakest (0.4408/0.4836), and roughly flat on activity_q1 users with only a handful of impressions. If pairwise FM lands inside noise of 0.6016, then combined with the failed lambdarank node (n004, 0.5986) the loss-mismatch story is falsified for this dataset, and the remaining headroom must be sought in model class (LHUC/SENet gating on DeepFM) and in ensembling genuinely decorrelated families rather than in further objective variants. [ref: BPR — Rendle 2009; LambdaRank]
